## Purpose and Entry Points
PR-Agent is a Python AI pull-request agent that runs review-oriented commands (`/review`, `/describe`, `/improve`, `/ask`, etc.) against pull requests or local diffs. Primary invocation paths are the CLI (`pr_agent/cli.py`, `pr_agent/cli_pip.py`), GitHub Action (`action.yaml`, `github_action/entrypoint.sh`), and provider-specific webhook/app servers under `pr_agent/servers/`.

## Command Routing and Tool Execution
`PRAgent` is the central dispatcher: it maps incoming commands/events to tool implementations and coordinates provider and configuration state. Each tool owns its prompt construction, LLM call, result parsing, and publication behavior.
- `pr_agent/agent/pr_agent.py`
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_reviewer.py`
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_code_suggestions.py`
- `pr_agent/tools/pr_description.py`

## Git-Provider Boundary
A provider abstraction normalizes PR URLs, diffs, files, comments, labels, and publishing operations across GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps, Gitea, Gerrit, CodeCommit, and local/plain-diff modes. Tool logic should depend on this boundary rather than platform SDK details.
- `pr_agent/git_providers/git_provider.py`
- `pr_agent/git_providers/github_provider.py`
- `pr_agent/git_providers/gitlab_provider.py`
- `pr_agent/git_providers/plain_diff_provider.py`

## Diff, Context, and Token Pipeline
Before model invocation, the system fetches and filters changed files, processes patches, derives language/context data, and fits content into model token budgets. This is the main scale boundary for large PRs; it produces compressed/dynamically selected context rather than passing raw repository state directly to an LLM.
- `pr_agent/algo/pr_processing.py`
- `pr_agent/algo/git_patch_processing.py`
- `pr_agent/algo/repo_context.py`
- `pr_agent/algo/token_handler.py`

## AI Model Integration
AI calls are isolated behind handlers, supporting direct OpenAI, LangChain, and LiteLLM-backed providers/models. Tools supply prompts and structured expectations; handlers execute completions and support provider/model selection and fallback-related behavior.
- `pr_agent/algo/ai_handlers/base_ai_handler.py`
- `pr_agent/algo/ai_handlers/litellm_ai_handler.py`
- `pr_agent/algo/ai_handlers/openai_ai_handler.py`

## Configuration, Prompts, and Secrets
Runtime behavior is configuration-driven: base settings and per-tool prompt templates are packaged in TOML, then loaded and potentially merged with repository-specific configuration. Secret-provider adapters support external secret retrieval, keeping credentials outside core tool workflows.
- `pr_agent/config_loader.py`
- `pr_agent/settings/configuration.toml`
- `pr_agent/settings/pr_reviewer_prompts.toml`
- `pr_agent/secret_providers/secret_provider.py`

## Event Hosting and Deployment
Servers translate platform webhooks, app events, polling, Actions execution, or Lambda requests into the common command-routing flow. Deployment supports Python/CLI environments, Docker, GitHub Actions, and serverless/webhook hosting; Gunicorn is included for hosted Python service operation.
- `pr_agent/servers/github_app.py`
- `pr_agent/servers/github_lambda_webhook.py`
- `pr_agent/servers/gitlab_webhook.py`
- `docker/Dockerfile`

## Mosaico Integration
The `mosaico` package is a separate service-facing integration layer with dispatch, execution, provider registration, observability, and an HTTP server. It appears to expose PR-Agent capabilities through Mosaico/A2A-oriented runtime contracts, distinct from direct Git-provider webhooks.
- `pr_agent/mosaico/server.py`
- `pr_agent/mosaico/dispatch.py`
- `pr_agent/mosaico/executor.py`
- `docker/mosaico/docker-compose.pr-agent.yml`
